newsitem.title: UK: UK's Lilley outlines three-point pension scheme.
newsitem.headline: UK's Lilley outlines three-point pension scheme.

text.p: British Social Security Secretary Peter Lilley on Wednesday outlined a three-point plan to reform state pensions.

Lilley said people in the new generation would have their own pension fund, would receive a rebate on national insurance contributions to be paid into that fund, and would have a state guarantee to ensure they received a pension at least equal to their basic state pension.
"We call the scheme "Basic Pension PLus'," Lilley told a news conference. "Because it is a basic pension, plus a fund, plus a rebate, plus a state guarantee."
Lilley said each fund should grow to provide the basic pension, but added that if a fund was insufficient, the state would top up the pension.
"No-one will do less well than under the present state scheme," he said.

He said government's actuary had calculated that a rebate of nine pounds a week would be needed to build up a fund big enough to pay a basic pension. This would be paid back from national insurance contributions.
